earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only survey/classification and ethnographic notes (Voorhoeve 1980 Asmat survey; Feuilleteau de Bruyn 1913/1915); no grammar or phonology of this variety found.

sources.citation: Drabbe, P. 1963. Drie Asmat-dialecten. Verhandelingen KITLV 42. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff. viii+236 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 9 p. 13 'De klemtoon': stress rule for Kawenak/Keenok/Keenakap (= Central Asmat, cent2117/yaos1235) only; Momogo/Pupis/Irogo were never surveyed by Drabbe. Not a North Asmat source.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: two refs, both 'a wordlist or less' (Voorhoeve 1980; Feuilleteau de Bruyn 1913); alt names North Asmat, Keenok; links to three lexibank 'Asmat, Central (Keenok..)' wordlists and Wikipedia.

sources.citation: Usher, T. & Suter, E. 2020. The Asmat-Muli languages of Southwestern New Guinea. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 38: 148-175.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 153 tree lists North Asmat [1,000 speakers 1991] as a language separate from Central Asmat (dialects Kawenak, Keenok, Keenakap, Sokoni); p. 154: 'The major source for the other languages and dialects is Voorhoeve's (1980) monograph'.

sources.citation: Pawley, A. & Hammarström, H. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In B. Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Documentation inventory only: 'Momogo-Pupis-Irogo [nks] 1,000; wordlist: Feuilleteau de Bruyn 1913, 1915, Voorhoeve 1980'. No stress data.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1980. The Asmat languages of Irian Jaya. Pacific Linguistics B-64. Canberra: ANU. x+177 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 4 'North Asmat' pp. 31-34 (PDF 41-44) is wordlist-based only; sec. 4.2 p. 32: 'The NA data have not yet been phonemicised; my impression is that the sound system of NA is identical to the KN system with the exception that [r] possibly is an allophone of /t/'. Sec. 3.1.2.3 p. 22 and sec. 7.2 p. 43: stress and pitch studied only in the KW dialect of Central Asmat and in Citak. No statement about North Asmat stress.

sources.citation: transnewguinea.org, 'Asmat, North' language page (Greenhill), citing van der Wouw, A. 1974. The Asmat people of the Casuarinen Coast. Irian 3: 1-20
sources.note: 27 lexical items, no phonology; labelled 'also Keenok'; the cited source is a Casuarina Coast Asmat article, so the attribution to nks is a mislabel.
Dialects Momogo (Mumugu), Pupis, Irogo (Eroko); notes population 'may include speakers of Keenok, classified as a Central Asmat dialect'; sole source Ethnologue 18. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Eberhard, D. M., Simons, G. F. & Fennig, C. D. (eds). Ethnologue: Languages of the World, entry 'Asmat, North' [nks] (18th ed. 2015 and later)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Only way to settle whether ISO nks (Ethnologue 'North Asmat') is Voorhoeve's Momogo-Pupis-Irogo or is being conflated with the Keenok dialect of Central Asmat (Glottolog/transnewguinea.org attach 'Keenok' to nort2917; Wikipedia says the population 'may include speakers of Keenok'); no stress data expected.

sources.citation: Trenkenschuh, F. A. (ed.) 1970. An annotated translation of 'De sociale struktuur van de Asmat bevolking' (G. Zegwaard & J. Boelaars). Asmat Sketch Book 1: 17-47. Hastings, NE: Crosier Missions.

sources.note: Voorhoeve's (1980:31) source for the claim that Sagapo speech is 'different from but still, with difficulty, understood by Keenok speakers'; ethnographic; useful for identity only.

sources.citation: Eyde, D. B. 1967. Cultural correlates of warfare among the Asmat of South-west New Guinea. Ph.D. thesis, Yale University. Ann Arbor: University Microfilms.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Eyde collected the Momogo wordlist that underlies Voorhoeve's North Asmat chapter (Voorhoeve 1980:4 n. 6); the thesis might carry the transcription conventions (accent marks) of that list; anthropological, so a stress statement is unlikely.

sources.citation: Drabbe, P. 1958. Grammar of the Keenok dialect. Mbi-Tsjiweu (mimeo); and Drabbe, P. n.d. Keenok-English dictionary (Dutch compiled, English translation)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Relevant only if ISO nks is taken to include Keenok (see identity note); Usher & Suter 2020:154 cite it as the only grammar of the Keenok dialect; linguistically it is Central Asmat (cent2117), so any stress statement there would belong to that entry, not nort2917.
